questions_and_answers.question: Where are tickets for major plays, sports, movies, etc. usually available?

answers.answer: At puree gaido (play guides), located in department stores and other major shopping areas
Only at the venue's box office
At train stations only
At the American Embassy

questions_and_answers.question: How are expressions for buying entertainment tickets different from buying train tickets?

answers.answer: They are similar, except that you have to specify the date
They are completely different
You must specify the seat number only
You do not need to specify anything

questions_and_answers.question: How do you ask for 'Three tickets for (the performance) on the 15th'?

answers.answer: 15-nichi no kippu 3-mai onegai shimasu.
15-nichi no kippu 3-ji onegai shimasu.
3-nichi no kippu 15-mai onegai shimasu.
15-nichi no kippu o mi ni ikimasen ka?

questions_and_answers.question: In the case of plays, what are the two performances per day called?

answers.answer: hiru no bu (afternoon performance) and yoru no bu (evening performance)
gozen no bu and gogo no bu
asa no bu and ban no bu
shitee-seki and jiyuu-seki

questions_and_answers.question: How do you ask 'Do you have tickets available for the afternoon performance on the 10th?'

answers.answer: Tooka no hiru no bu no kippu wa arimasu ka?
Tooka no yoru no bu no kippu wa arimasu ka?
Tooka no hiru no bu no kippu 3-mai onegai shimasu.
Tooka no hiru no bu ni shimashoo ka?

questions_and_answers.question: Why must you specify which performance when buying a ticket for a play?

answers.answer: Because there are two performances per day (afternoon and evening)
Because tickets are sold only at department stores
Because plays have no reserved seats
Because the date is not printed on the ticket

articles.text:
4. Buying tickets

Tickets for major plays, sports, movies, etc. are usually available at puree gaido (play guides), which are located in department stores and other major shopping areas.

The expressions used in buying tickets for entertainment are similar to those used when buying train tickets except that you have to specify the date. Look at the following example:

15-nichi no kippu 3-mai onegai shimasu.    Three tickets for (the performance) on the 15th.

In some cases, especially in the case of plays, there are two performances per day, the afternoon performance (hiru no bu) and the evening performance (yoru no bu). Therefore, when you buy such a ticket, you will have to specify which performance you want a ticket for. Look at the following example:

Tooka no hiru no bu no kippu wa arimasu ka?    Do you have tickets available for the afternoon performance on the 10th?
